subtopic: Using AI tools for learning without cheating
subtype: Approach: testing understanding without the tool [Revision]
passage: Tutor's note, Hemant. Mridul came in on Thursday and said something I liked: “I notice I open the AI before I try the problem.” He had decided to test himself. He closed it, took a fresh problem like last week's, and tried it cold for fifteen minutes. He got stuck at the second step and saw that he could not remember how to set up the equation, something he had let the tool do all month. He wrote down the gap and set a rule for himself: a fair attempt first, twenty minutes; only then ask for a hint, never the answer. We went over the gap together. Next week he will show me his attempts before asking for help. I told him that noticing this on his own is the harder part.

qa.q: How long did Mridul try the problem without the tool?
qa.a: Mridul tried it cold for fifteen minutes.

qa.q: How does Mridul probably feel on seeing the gap?
qa.a: Mridul probably feels uneasy but honest, and determined to fix it, since he wrote down the gap and set a rule.

qa.q: What could Mridul do to make the rule stick?
qa.a: Mridul could show his attempts to Hemant and note where a hint was needed, since a record keeps the habit honest.

qa.q: How might Hemant see Mridul's self-test?
qa.a: Hemant is encouraged, since noticing the dependence alone is the harder part.

grounding: After noticing he depends on AI, a student closes it, tries a similar problem cold, sees gaps and asks for hints only after a fair attempt.
